title.en: Valid XML is not correct data: schema and data-quality checks

description.en: Check a FundsXML delivery in two steps with FreeXmlToolkit: the FundsXML schema finds a wrong data type, the FundsXML data-quality checks find position weights that add up to 120 percent although the file is valid.

say.en: In this video you check a FundsXML delivery in two steps: against the schema, and against the rules of the business. It takes about three minutes.

A fund administrator has sent this file: the month-end portfolio of an equity fund. The root element is FundsXML4, and the first lines name the schema, FundsXML4.xsd. So FreeXmlToolkit can validate it right away.
Press F8. The schema checks the structure and the data types of every element. The Problems panel below the editor lists an error.
Click the problem. The caret jumps to the market value of the first position. An amount must be a decimal number, but someone has written it out in words.

Type the number instead, nine million three hundred seventy-five thousand, and press F8 again. The error is gone. What is left are hints, in blue: the derivatives in this portfolio could also report their exposure. Hints are suggestions, not mistakes.
Now a second delivery of the same fund. It passes the schema without a single error. Every element is in its place, every number is a number.
But the Problems panel shows two warnings. They come from the FundsXML data-quality checks: the weights of the positions add up to one hundred and twenty percent.

Click the warning about the first position. It claims twenty-eight point three three percent, but its value is only eight point three three percent of the fund's net asset value. Correct the weight and validate again. Both warnings are gone.

The green FundsXML mark in the status bar shows that the document was recognised. With it come more than fifty checks: ISIN and LEI check digits, currency codes, dates, position values against the net asset value, and many more. A schema tells you whether a file is well formed. These checks tell you whether its data can be right.
Thanks for watching. That was checking a FundsXML file in two steps. The schema, the example files and the documentation are free to use: the links are on the screen and in the description below.
